results.title: The supplied call date produces two different product deadlines

results.meaning: Each product uses its own lateness band. Business-day counts are strictly after today; the listed holidays are skipped. Node totals describe these fixtures, not a universal graph size.

results.title: Past days, weekends, holidays and a day after the deadline
results.meaning: The suggestion is computed by the local reference-style snippet. A valid business day can still be too late for this product. This helper's verdict is separate from speaking to a customer.

results.title: Percentage, fixed, composite and rounded floors
results.meaning: The rule combines all available candidates with max by default or min when requested; generated floors are capped at the debt. Rounding happens in cents, after percentage precision is scaled to three decimal places.

results.title: A typed lateness row overrides the untyped row
results.meaning: Both products have the same lateness, yet the card gets the card-specific deadline. Omitting the type from a reference helper does not test this override.

results.title: 36500 account cents becomes 365.00; a spoken 120.50 becomes integer 12050
results.meaning: The model supplies major currency units; coercion adapts the API request to integer cents. This requires recognizable field roles/minor-unit cues and assumes 100 minor units per currency unit.

results.title: A legal amount/date passes without a stored customer yes
results.kind: executed hook plus compiled prompt inspection

output.prompt_readback: 8. Read back the product, the amount and the date and ask exactly "Do you confirm?". Call create_promise only after a clear yes. If they change the date or the amount, check it with rules 3 and 4 and read back again.

results.meaning: The prompt requires a clear yes; the hard guard validates product/date/amount and duplicate state. This output does not establish consent. There is still no deterministic customer-confirmation ledger binding this request.

results.title: HTTP success is separated from the bank's negative acknowledgment
results.meaning: Current setup initializes the ack counter, so a bank refusal does not select promise. The outcome snippet deliberately falls back to the engine success counter if the ack variable is missing; that corrupted/legacy state can still select promise. Counters in this example are supplied by the local batch double.

results.title: A parallel promise batch with one 5xx recovers on retry

output.duplicate_guard: blocked: a promise for p2 is already recorded and cannot be changed or recorded again

results.meaning: Acknowledged counts rise immediately, while per-product batch attribution waits for a complete acknowledged batch/retry. The correct retry commits the held products; another promise for a committed product is blocked. However, retrying p2 instead of the failed p1 also completes the held batch: the algorithm counts retried keys without proving which original call failed. It then marks p1 despite no positive result for p1 in this probe. The helper deliberately models all pre-hooks before post-hooks.

results.title: Note batches preserve their reason and reject later forbidden notes

output.second_note_guard: blocked: a note for p2 is already saved

results.meaning: In this probe, the initial mixed batch commits no note attribution; the supported retry completes it. Current note guards reject a second acknowledged note, a note for a promised product and a lean note after transfer when notes_on_transfer is false. Closing takes the first non-paid reason in account order.

results.meaning: The current compiler wires a callback guard after coercion. With setup's slot table it blocks wrong days/times and a slot equal to now. With no slots (including custom rules or skipped setup) it permits the request. Both the complete chain and standalone guard permit 11:99 and 12:60: their shape and lexical range pass despite invalid minutes. The helper calls those times unreadable. This supersedes the older claim that callbacks have no hard guard.

results.title: Identity normalizes answers and tracks progress without all_verified
results.meaning: DMY normalization converts the numeric birth date; digit normalization joins the phone digits. The current hook tracks distinct verified questions and sets identity_all_verified. The compiler can route on that flag; collecting complete answers and question order still require the model. The tracking queue assumes results arrive in request order.

results.title: A dropped transition marker is consumed once
results.meaning: The ending target is sent through a fixed-goodbye recovery path; a third-party move back to identity is recovered directly. The response becomes handled, preventing a repeat on the next pass. Only targets actually exposed as transition tools are candidates. This executes repository recovery code, not the remote platform transition engine.

results.title: A fixed sentence under an unknown extra key reaches the scoped prompt

input.sentence: I will now pass you to a colleague.

inserted_lines: - [X-EXAMPLE-PH] Before transferring, say exactly: "I will now pass you to a colleague."
notes: rule is said by no node of the workflow; it is placed word for word in negotiate

results.meaning: The rescue adds an instruction and a rule-map location; it does not make this an actual spoken transcript. Presence is an unordered ASCII token test over all compiled strings, so code comments/wrong context and non-Latin wording expose false assurance limits.

results.title: Date-cue fixing can abstain or flatten ambiguous English

output.text: Propose the 2nd business day after today or the 3rd business day after today.
Propose the last business day of this week or the last business day of next week.
Propose the next business day, unless that is after the deadline.

results.meaning: Tomorrow is treated as next business day without consulting a calendar; alternatives within one family can collapse to the first match. Additional deadline conditions can cause abstention. Fixing and validation share this heuristic, so consistency is not semantic proof.

results.title: Support/human offer branches are prompts; the hardship exit gate is code
results.kind: compiled prompt inspection plus executed exit gate

output.support_bullet: - Mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss: Say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt. If the customer still names a date or an amount, record the promise under the date and amount rules. Offer to connect them with the customer support team. Make this offer only once. Make no other offer of any kind (no other transfer, plan or discount) unless the customer explicitly asks for it. If they accept or insist (yes, or any clear agreement): say you will transfer them, say goodbye and call transition_to_handoff_support. If they clearly decline: thank them, say goodbye and call transition_to_end_hardship - do not ask again. If they ask a question about the offer (for example what it would help with), ask for time, make small talk or say something cut off, it is neither a yes nor a no: answer briefly from the facts you have (say so if you do not know), keep the offer open and wait; do not ask it again. This is not a refusal and not a second offer: do not transfer, add a note or end the call because of it. If the next reply is still neither a clear yes nor a clear no, take it as a decline. Once this applies, it comes before the rules for flat_refusal, restructuring: never make a persuasion attempt and never transfer the customer to the restructuring team in this call. [A-32a, A-32b, A-32c, A-32d, +1]
output.human_bullet: - Asks for a human: Ask once whether you can help first. If they insist: say you will transfer them, say goodbye and call transition_to_handoff_general. If they let you help, go on; do not offer it again. [A-42a, A-42b, A-45c]

results.meaning: Support has accept/decline/clarify branches and waits without repeating the offer. Accepting assistant help is different from insisting on a human transfer. These are prompt branches, not observed replies. Once the model-recognized hardship latch is yes, the code blocks restructuring; recognition remains model-dependent.

results.title: Joint confirmation and closing every product
results.kind: compiled prompt inspection plus executed outcome code

joint_prompt_lines: B4. When EVERY product is agreed or refused: read back all agreed promises together in ONE message (the product, the amount and the date of each, and any date moved to a deadline) and ask "Do you confirm?" once. After the yes, call create_promise for each agreed product, one call at a time, without asking again in between. If they change one, check it and read all of them back again.

8. Read back only as in B4: once, for all products together, and ask exactly "Do you confirm?". Call create_promise only after a clear yes. If they change the date or the amount, check it with rules 3 and 4 and read back again.

11. After a promise is recorded, call create_promise for the next product of the joint read-back at once. Say that the promises are recorded and the sentence above once, after the last one. Only when every product is handled, follow B8 to thank the customer, say goodbye and close.

results.meaning: The joint readback/one-confirmation rule is now consistent across the prompt and success hook, but consent still has no hard ledger. All-paid needs a paid note for every known product; an unnoted product is not proved paid. A failed transfer still selects transferred because the supplied policy has no transfer-failed outcome.
